title: Razorpay Builds India's First AI Payments Foundation Model With NVIDIA and AWS
excerpt: The fintech giant's new model, trained on over 4 billion transactions, aims to sharpen payment routing and fraud detection across India's digital payments ecosystem.
body:
• Razorpay has launched what it calls India's first AI-powered payments foundation model, built in partnership with NVIDIA and Amazon Web Services.
  • The model has been trained on data from over 4 billion transactions processed through Razorpay's platform, targeting payment routing optimization and fraud detection.
  • The initiative builds on Razorpay's broader push into AI-native commerce, including agentic payments with OpenAI and its MCP server infrastructure.
  • India processes over 20 billion UPI transactions monthly, making intelligent payment routing a critical capability for reducing the estimated ₹7,000 crore in annual losses from transaction failures.

Razorpay has unveiled what it describes as India's first AI-powered payments foundation model, developed in collaboration with NVIDIA and Amazon Web Services. The model, trained on data from more than 4 billion transactions processed through the company's platform, is designed to optimize payment routing and strengthen fraud detection across India's rapidly expanding digital payments infrastructure.

What the Model Does

The foundation model targets two of the most persistent pain points in India's digital payments ecosystem: transaction failures and fraud. Indian businesses currently lose an estimated ₹7,000 crore annually to failed transactions, according to Razorpay's own data. Server downtime, service degradation, and suboptimal routing between payment gateways and banks contribute to failure rates that can cost merchants up to 30 percent of potential revenue.

https://x.com/Razorpay/status/2089611061372780717

The AI model analyzes hundreds of parameters in real time to determine the optimal payment gateway for each transaction. By learning from patterns across billions of historical transactions, it can predict which routing path is most likely to succeed for a given payment method, bank, amount, and time of day.

On the fraud detection side, the model is trained to identify suspicious patterns that traditional rule-based systems miss, including behavioral anomalies, unusual device fingerprints, and velocity attacks that exploit gaps between authorization and settlement windows.

The Technology Stack

NVIDIA's GPU infrastructure provides the computing backbone for training and running the model. AWS supplies the cloud environment where the model operates at scale, handling the throughput demands of a platform that processes more than 5,000 transactions per second at peak load.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=MsyZQHvyEiM

The partnership reflects a growing trend among Indian fintech companies to build proprietary AI models rather than rely on general-purpose large language models for specialized financial tasks. Payment routing and fraud scoring require low-latency, high-precision inference that general AI models are not optimized to deliver.

Razorpay's Broader AI Push

The foundation model is the latest move in Razorpay's aggressive expansion into AI-native commerce. In October 2025, the company partnered with OpenAI and the National Payments Corporation of India to launch agentic payments on ChatGPT, allowing AI systems to discover products, build carts, and complete UPI transactions on behalf of users.

Earlier in 2026, Razorpay launched India's first payment gateway MCP server for instant AI integration and introduced a command-line interface for developers building in AI-powered coding environments like OpenAI Codex and Anthropic's Claude. The company has also deployed an AI-powered Optimizer that uses real-time data across over 100 payment integrations to route transactions dynamically.

What It Means for India's Payments Landscape

India now processes over 20 billion UPI transactions per month, making it one of the world's largest real-time payment markets. As transaction volumes continue to surge, even small improvements in routing success rates translate into billions of rupees recovered for merchants.

The company completed its reverse flip — redomiciling back to India from the United States — and is set to return to profitability in FY26, according to CEO Harshil Mathur. With its $852 million valuation and full-stack fintech ambitions spanning payments, banking, lending, and now AI infrastructure, Razorpay is positioning itself as the operating system for India's digital commerce economy.

For NRIs and cross-border users, the model's improvements in transaction success rates could reduce the friction and failed payments that have long plagued international remittances and e-commerce purchases routed through Indian payment gateways.
